content.title: About
content.content: Duck is a waterfowl raised for its meat. Roasted duck with crispy skin is a delicacy in many world cuisines. The skin is rich in fat, which when properly cooked becomes aromatic and crunchy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ducks are capable of migration, but most commercial birds are kept on closed farms.
Duck skin is high in collagen, which forms a golden crust during prolonged roasting.
In China, Peking duck is a classic dish where the skin is the star of the flavor.
Duck fat is prized for frying and in cosmetics because of its softening properties.
Duck meat contains more iron than chicken.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Duck meat provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: The iron in duck meat is readily absorbed and helps maintain healthy hemoglobin levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Duck supplies B12, niacin, and riboflavin, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Polyunsaturated fats
items.content: Duck fat contains omega‑6 and modest amounts of omega‑3 fatty acids, beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Collagen in the skin
items.content: When roasted, the skin releases collagen, which may aid skin elasticity and joint health.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Duck skin is very fatty; overconsumption can lead to excess calories and elevated cholesterol.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Undercooked duck may harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter; cook to an internal temperature of 165 °F (74 °C).

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to bird meat.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Duck is high in purines, which can be problematic for people with gout.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Duck can be roasted whole, cut into portions, or used cold in salads. The skin is eaten crispy, seasoned with salt, spices, or a glaze. Serve with fruit sauces, vegetable sides, or traditional Chinese pancakes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked roasted duck in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in bags at –18 °C, where it keeps quality for 2‑3 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 165 °F (74 °C) before eating.
